places.title: Victoria Memorial
places.description: Iconic marble building dedicated to Queen Victoria, surrounded by expansive gardens and lush green lawns.

places.title: Indian Museum
places.description: The oldest and largest multi-purpose museum in the Asia-Pacific region, housing rare antiques, mummies, and armor.

places.title: Howrah Bridge & Flower Market
places.description: Famous cantilever bridge spanning the Hooghly river alongside the colorful Mullick Ghat Flower Market.

places.title: Birla Planetarium
places.description: Single-storied circular structure designed in the Buddhist Stupa style featuring daily astronomy shows.

places.title: Park Street Culinary Walk & Peter Cat
places.description: Legendary street famed for iconic Chelo Kebabs, heritage cafes, and Kolkata street food delights.

places.title: Dakshineswar Kali Temple & Belur Math
places.description: Spiritual center on the banks of Hooghly River founded by Rani Rashmoni, connected to Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.

places.title: Science City Kolkata
places.description: Largest science center in the Indian subcontinent featuring space theater, 3D digital shows, and time ride.

places.title: Marble Palace Mansion
places.description: Palatial 19th-century mansion built with ninety-six types of marble, housing classical European sculptures.

places.title: Eco Tourism Park
places.description: Sprawling urban park with replica 7 Wonders of the World, boating lake, and ecological zones.

places.title: Academy of Fine Arts & Nandan
places.description: Cultural hub of Kolkata hosting theatrical performances, art exhibitions, and film screenings.

places.title: St. Paul's Cathedral
places.description: Magnificent Gothic Revival cathedral renowned for its stained glass windows, serene nave, and peaceful gardens.

places.title: Princep Ghat & River Promenade
places.description: Palladian porch monument along the banks of River Hooghly offering traditional wooden boat rides at sunset.

places.title: Jorasanko Thakur Bari
places.description: Ancestral home and museum of Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore, showcasing Bengal renaissance literature and art.

places.title: South Park Street Cemetery
places.description: Atmospheric 18th-century colonial cemetery covered in mossy neoclassical and gothic obelisks amid tropical trees.

places.title: College Street Boi Para & Coffee House
places.description: World's largest second-hand book market paired with legendary adda debates at Indian Coffee House since 1942.

places.title: Mother House (Missionaries of Charity)
places.description: Global headquarters established by Mother Teresa, housing her tomb, preserved living quarters, and peaceful chapel.

places.title: Alipore Zoological Gardens
places.description: India's oldest formal zoological garden spread over 46 acres, home to migratory winter birds and Bengal tigers.

places.title: Netaji Bhawan & Museum
places.description: Memorial hall and research center preserving the life, historic escape vehicle, and belongings of Subhas Chandra Bose.

places.title: Kalighat Kali Temple
places.description: Ancient Shakti Peetha pilgrimage temple revered as one of the most sacred spiritual sanctuaries in eastern India.

places.title: Kolkata Town Hall & High Court Heritage
places.description: Roman-Doric colonial public hall built in 1813, showcasing high-tech interactive exhibits on Kolkata's evolution.

rag_context: Victoria Memorial entry tickets cost ₹50 for Indian nationals. The gardens are open early at 5:30 AM for morning walkers.
Indian Museum is located right next to Park Street Metro, ideal indoor shelter during monsoon rainstorms.
Park Street is Kolkata's premier culinary avenue with famous heritage restaurants like Peter Cat, Flurys, and Mocambo.
Howrah Bridge gets heavy traffic between 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM - 8:00 PM. Metro transit via Green Line under river is recommended.
Dakshineswar Kali Temple closes its main sanctum between 12:30 PM and 3:30 PM.

places.title: Eiffel Tower
places.description: Iconic wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, offering panoramic views of Paris.

places.title: Louvre Museum
places.description: The world's largest art museum and historic monument housing the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo.

places.title: Musée d'Orsay
places.description: Housed in a grand Beaux-Arts railway station featuring Impressionist masterpieces by Monet and Van Gogh.

places.title: Sainte-Chapelle & Conciergerie
places.description: Royal chapel in Gothic style with breathtaking 13th-century stained glass windows.

places.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral & Île de la Cité
places.description: Masterpiece of French Gothic architecture on an island in the Seine, renowned for its rose windows and twin towers.

places.title: Arc de Triomphe & Champs-Élysées
places.description: Monumental triumphal arch honoring French military victories, crowning the world-famous avenue.

places.title: Sacré-Cœur Basilica & Montmartre
places.description: White Romano-Byzantine basilica perched atop Montmartre hill overlooking Paris alongside Bohemian artist squares.

places.title: Centre Pompidou Modern Art
places.description: Radical inside-out high-tech architecture housing Europe's premier collection of modern and contemporary art.

places.title: Palais Garnier Opera House
places.description: Opulent 19th-century opera house with sweeping marble Grand Staircase and ceiling painted by Marc Chagall.

places.title: Luxembourg Gardens & Medici Fountain
places.description: Tranquil 25-hectare formal palace gardens with tree-lined promenades, model sailboats, and classical statues.

places.title: Panthéon & Latin Quarter
places.description: Neoclassical dome in the Latin Quarter serving as the mausoleum for Voltaire, Rousseau, Victor Hugo, and Marie Curie.

places.title: Musée de l'Orangerie
places.description: Intimate impressionist gallery inside Tuileries Garden featuring Claude Monet's complete Water Lilies cycle murals.

places.title: Le Marais Culinary & Pastry Walk
places.description: Chic historic district with artisan boulangeries, gourmet macarons, falafel bars on Rue des Rosiers, and courtyards.

places.title: Seine River Sightseeing Cruise
places.description: Scenic glass-canopied boat cruise drifting past Pont Alexandre III, Musée d'Orsay, and the bridges of Paris.

places.title: Musée Rodin & Rose Garden
places.description: Elegant 18th-century mansion and sculpture garden showcasing The Thinker and The Gates of Hell by Auguste Rodin.

places.title: Tuileries Garden & Place de la Concorde
places.description: Historic public garden connecting the Louvre with Place de la Concorde, framed by fountains and sculptured avenues.

places.title: Galeries Lafayette Haussmann & Glass Dome
places.description: Grand department store renowned for its neo-Byzantine stained-glass cupola and rooftop terrace views across Paris.

places.title: Paris Catacombs
places.description: Underground ossuaries holding the remains of over six million Parisians in a subterranean labyrinth of stone tunnels.

places.title: Grand Palais & Petit Palais
places.description: Historic Beaux-Arts exhibition halls with colossal glass vaulted roofs housing fine art collections and classical salons.

places.title: Père Lachaise Cemetery
places.description: World's most visited garden cemetery, resting place of Oscar Wilde, Frédéric Chopin, Édith Piaf, and Jim Morrison.

rag_context: The Louvre Museum requires timed entry reservations in advance. Tuesday is closed day.
The Eiffel Tower summit elevator can be paused during strong winds or rain.
Musée d'Orsay offers free audio guides with masterworks breakdown.
Paris metro tickets can be loaded onto Navigo Easy smart cards for convenient subway transfers.
Sainte-Chapelle is best viewed on sunny mornings when sunlight illuminates the upper stained-glass chapel.

places.title: Senso-ji Temple
places.description: Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple located in Asakusa with Nakamise shopping street.

places.title: teamLab Planets
places.description: Immersive body-on digital art museum where visitors walk through water and light installations.

places.title: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Yoyogi Park
places.description: Serene Shinto shrine surrounded by 170 acres of evergreen forest in the heart of Harajuku.

places.title: Shibuya Crossing & Hachiko Square
places.description: World's busiest pedestrian scramble crossing surrounded by colossal video screens and neon lights.

places.title: Tokyo Skytree Observation Deck
places.description: The tallest tower in the world reaching 634 meters, with panoramic vistas stretching to Mount Fuji on clear days.

places.title: Akihabara Electric Town & Retro Games
places.description: Vibrant center for electronics, manga, multi-story arcade centers, and anime subculture collectibles.

places.title: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
places.description: Sprawling historic park blending traditional Japanese landscape, English landscape, and French formal garden styles.

places.title: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
places.description: Bustling foodie haven packed with sushi bars, grilled wagyu skewers, tamagoyaki omelet stands, and fresh oysters.

places.title: Roppongi Hills & Mori Art Museum
places.description: Contemporary art museum perched on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower featuring cutting-edge exhibitions.

places.title: Tokyo National Museum (Ueno Park)
places.description: Japan's oldest national museum housing comprehensive treasures of samurai swords, kimonos, scrolls, and pottery.

places.title: Imperial Palace East Gardens
places.description: Historic stone walls, watchtowers, and manicured lawns built upon the former foundations of Edo Castle.

places.title: Odaiba Waterfront & Gundam Statue
places.description: Futuristic island in Tokyo Bay boasting life-sized Unicorn Gundam, Rainbow Bridge vistas, and coastal promenades.

places.title: Ginza Luxury Avenue & Kabuki-za Theater
places.description: Premier shopping and theater district showcasing traditional Japanese Kabuki classical drama performances.

places.title: Harajuku Takeshita Street & Cat Street
places.description: Pulse of Japanese youth fashion, street crêpes, indie vintage boutiques, and quirky concept stores.

places.title: Tokyo Tower & Zojo-ji Temple
places.description: Classic red-and-white communications tower standing in harmony next to ancient Edo-era temple grounds.

places.title: Yanaka Ginza Old Tokyo Heritage Walk
places.description: Charming preserved neighborhood that survived WWII, famous for retro wooden storefronts, tea shops, and street cats.

places.title: Miraikan National Museum of Emerging Science
places.description: High-tech science museum featuring interactive robotics, humanoid displays, Earth simulators, and space science.

places.title: Omoide Yokocho & Shinjuku Golden Gai
places.description: Nostalgic labyrinth of narrow alleyways crammed with tiny yakitori stalls, ramen counters, and micro-bars.

places.title: Nezu Shrine & Azalea Garden
places.description: Historic 18th-century Shinto shrine celebrated for its vibrant red Torii tunnel path and tranquil hillside greenery.

places.title: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum
places.description: Remarkable collection of preserved historic buildings, tea houses, and vintage public bathhouses from old Edo.

rag_context: teamLab Planets requires barefoot entry; water levels reach knee-high in certain art rooms.
Senso-ji Nakamise stalls close around 6:00 PM, though the temple grounds stay lit at night.
Suica/Pasmo IC cards make Tokyo subway navigation instant and seamless.
Shibuya Sky rooftop tickets should be booked for sunset times 4 weeks in advance.
Tsukiji Outer Market operates primarily in the morning hours from 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM.
